In 2005, Oprah Winfrey financed the construction of 65 homes in Houston for families displaced by Hurricane Katrina, creating Angel Lane as a community for evacuees. Over time, the neighborhood faced challenges such as crime concerns, disputes among residents, and delays in building a promised community center, which finally opened eight years later, providing essential services and support for the residents. Despite the difficulties, the project succeeded in helping families find housing and rebuild their lives after the disaster.

 - Oprah Winfrey committed $10 million to build homes for hurricane evacuees in Houston.
 - Residents of Angel Lane faced various challenges including crime, community disagreements, and delays in the promised community center.
 - The long-awaited community center opened eight years after the first families moved in, aiming to foster community ties and provide essential services.
